qs.q:
Work Experiences — Which person…

A=Amelia (personal shopper, planned shopping schedule, awkward/personal tasks, had to borrow clothes from parents, successful job as dropout architecture student)
B=Ben (homemade chocolates, fed up commuting, attended a course, learned new techniques from expert, proud of success; former factory failed)

0. got a job instead of his friend? [F=Finley: 'I volunteered after my friend had to quit']
1. at first felt uncomfortable during their job?
2. found it quite easy to change their work routine?
3. followed the advice of a professional?
4. says they depended on help from a partner?
5. abandoned their career plan?
6. had to make difficult choices?
7. started working for free?
8. quit their job?
9. earned enough to return their debts?
10. needed special equipment?
11. spent more money than they intended?
12. wishes they had not chosen that line of work?
items: 1 — at first felt uncomfortable during their job?
2 — found it quite easy to change their work routine?
3 — followed the advice of a professional?
4 — says they depended on help from a partner?
9 — earned enough to return their debts?
11 — spent more money than they intended?

qs.q:
Robot Future

"you take the best and brightest 200 human beings, you scan and copy their brains to get robots that... are INDIVISIBLE FROM THE HUMANS on which they are based."

Robin Hanson thinks that the robot takeover will…
A come soon.
B require 200 robots.
C depend on imitating.
D expand the labour market.

Robot Future

"The Ems, being modelled on us, will share some combination of GRATITUDE, EMPATHY AND AFFECTION FOR HUMANS."

The Ems will not kill us because…
A they won't need to.
B they will be capable of feeling for us.
C they will want to share with us.
D they will not be sophisticated enough.
opts: they will be capable of feeling for us.
they will want to share with us.
they will not be sophisticated enough.

qs.q:
Robot Future

"humans who... spend their time DOING NOTHING MUCH AND STARING AT SCREENS."

According to the author…
A in the future robots will rule the world.
B humans are predicted to lack empathy.
C only particular skills will be required.
D humans will have too much time on their hands.
opts: in the future robots will rule the world.
humans are predicted to lack empathy.
only particular skills will be required.
humans will have too much time on their hands.

qs.q:
Robot Future

"to make Ems possible, only THREE TECHNOLOGIES need to coincide: faster computers; brain scanning; and the MODELLING OF THE HUMAN MIND."

Hansen says…
A the development of Ems does not depend on artificial intelligence.
B artificial intelligence is comprised of three technologies.
C the development of Ems depends largely on brain scanning.
D artificial intelligence is hard to predict.
opts: the development of Ems does not depend on artificial intelligence.
artificial intelligence is comprised of three technologies.
the development of Ems depends largely on brain scanning.
artificial intelligence is hard to predict.

qs.q:
Robot Future

"all the predictions lead to the same place: THE DISAPPEARANCE OF HUMAN LABOUR."

It is predicted that the robot future will cause…
A a world without work.
B 75% unemployment among drivers.
C the destruction of petrol stations.
D a resistance to the automation of everything.
opts: a resistance to the automation of everything.

qs.q:
Robot Future

"'Everyone can enjoy a life of serious leisure IF THE MACHINE-PRODUCED WEALTH IS SHARED, OR MOST PEOPLE CAN END UP MISERABLY POOR if the machine owners successfully lobby against wealth redistribution.'"

If we lived in a world without labour…
A wealth would be distributed fairly.
B we would all be miserably poorer.
C we would all be able to live a life of leisure.
D the distribution of wealth would determine the benefits.
opts: we would all be miserably poorer.
we would all be able to live a life of leisure.
the distribution of wealth would determine the benefits.

qs.q:
Why Yoga?

"When our usual hobbies like television and sports do not give us the kind of mental and spiritual relief we are looking for, we are forced to turn to traditional and holistic techniques of relaxation. (19) ____."

A However, in recent years, people have progressed a lot in accepting many traditional and oriental techniques for physical and spiritual healing.
B Thus, by practising yoga, a person is said to join with the Supreme Being.
C Eastern therapies are too often misunderstood in the west.
D And yoga's low-impact stretching and breathing is perfect for the less young among us.
E Such techniques are quickly catching up on the fast-moving masses.
F But yoga is about more than just the body, and these people grossly misunderstand its true power.
G In fact, yoga requires you to apply your intelligence in understanding its techniques.
H For example, hatha yoga focuses on postures to purify the body.
opts: A — in recent years people have progressed a lot in accepting traditional techniques
B — by practising yoga a person joins with the Supreme Being
C — Eastern therapies are too often misunderstood in the west
D — yoga's low-impact stretching is perfect for the less young
E — Such techniques are quickly catching up on the fast-moving masses
F — But yoga is about more than just the body
G — yoga requires you to apply your intelligence
H — For example, hatha yoga focuses on postures
